rulings.item: divergence 1 (fails_wrongly) at t=0 ms: The road user's velocity [-2.4, 14.3] has magnitude 14.5 m/s and absolute cosine exactly 0.6 with carrier direction [20, 21], meeting the inclusive threshold. Micrometre truncation in the direction reader slightly enlarges the normalised vector, causing the body to reject this boundary case. — contract: holds, body: fails; contract: "a is moving, its speed (kin.speed) above speed_tol, and its velocity (kin.velocity) makes with r's designated direction (st.lane_direction) an angle whose cosine, in absolute value, is at most cos_max"
rulings.why: The contract states its test as a dot product with "the normalised direction", and the atom contract for st.lane_direction defines that reading: the vector is the unit vector times a factor of at least 1, exactly the unit vector only where the scaled length is a whole number of micrometres. For [20, 21] that length is 29/21, which is not a whole number of micrometres, so the read vector is slightly longer than the unit vector. Under that disclosed reading, the dot product at this exact boundary (8.7 against 0.6 × 14.5) slightly exceeds cos_max times the speed, which gives the body's verdict. — "the absolute value of the dot product of the velocity with the normalised direction is at most cos_max times the speed"
